👶 Understanding IV Cannulation Through Scalp Veins in Newborns 👶

Seeing an IV line placed on a newborn's scalp can be concerning for parents, but it is a safe and commonly used medical practice in neonatal care.

Scalp vein cannulation is often performed when healthcare professionals need reliable intravenous access for:
✔ Fluids and hydration
✔ Medications
✔ Nutritional support
✔ Emergency treatment

The procedure is carefully performed by trained medical professionals using sterile techniques and appropriate monitoring.

It's important to know that the IV is placed in the scalp veins—not in the brain—and does not affect brain development or function.

Parental awareness and understanding can help reduce anxiety during a newborn's medical treatment.

Proud to share that the Department of Pediatrics, MGM Medical College Kamothe, successfully conducted the *Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) Course* on 2nd & 3rd May 2026! 

I had the wonderful experience of serving as *Course Coordinator* for this program. Organising it, watching 36 enthusiastic delegates, postgraduate students as well as Senior Pediatricians , dive into hands-on training in advanced life support was both rewarding and energising.

I’m also grateful to have served as an *Instructor for the IAP CPR (BLS) course* held on 14th April. It’s been an inspiring month of training and learning together as a team.

Huge thanks to our *Course Director, Dr. Gavhane Sir*, and to our 6 expert instructors who made the training impactful. Special gratitude to our Dean *Dr. Narshetty, and Medical Director Dr. Salgotra, for their invaluable support in making the course a success.

Events like these remind me why teaching and training the next generation of pediatricians is the best part of this work.

🌟 Delivered a talk on “Pediatric Red Flags: Recognising the Sick Child” today at *Sushrut Hospital & Research Centre,  Chembur* 🌟

Had the opportunity to speak at a well-organised **Pediatric CME** for General Practitioners and doctors from other specialities. The session focused on early identification of the seriously ill child — something that can truly make a difference in the first critical minutes of a consultation.

Through real-life case-based scenarios and active interaction, we discussed key clinical clues, often-missed signs, and practical decision-making pointers that help differentiate a stable child from one who needs urgent escalation. The enthusiastic participation and insightful questions from the audience made the session truly engaging.

A heartfelt thank you to the organising team at Sushrut Hospital for the kind invitation and excellent arrangements. Grateful to all the GPs, physicians, and specialists who attended and contributed so actively.

Early recognition remains one of the most powerful tools we have in pediatrics. Let’s continue to strengthen this bridge between primary care and intensive care for better outcomes in our children.

As part of my ongoing commitment to strengthening emergency response skills among healthcare professionals, I had the opportunity to conduct a Basic and Advanced Life Support Workshop for the nursing staff at *ACTREC, Tata Memorial Centre, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai*.

The workshop was focused on equipping nurses with structured, evidence-based approaches to managing cardiopulmonary emergencies.

A key highlight was the Nurses PALS (Pediatric Advanced Life Support) component, which emphasized:
🔹 Early recognition of respiratory distress and shock
🔹 High-quality CPR and effective team dynamics
🔹 Airway management and ventilation strategies
🔹 Timely intervention in pediatric cardiac arrest scenarios
🔹 Simulation-based training to enhance real-time decision-making

Nurses play a pivotal role as first responders in hospital settings, and empowering them with advanced resuscitation skills significantly improves patient outcomes—especially in time-critical situations.

It was truly encouraging to see the enthusiasm, precision, and dedication of the nursing team towards mastering these life-saving skills.

Together, through continuous training and preparedness, we move closer to delivering safer and more responsive healthcare.

Continuing my mission to spread awareness and empower the community with life-saving CPR skills, I had the privilege of conducting two meaningful training sessions:

The session saw enthusiastic participation from essential workers including housekeeping staff and security personnel, as well as residents across all age groups—from children to the elderly. It was heartening to witness such inclusive community engagement toward emergency preparedness.
Every trained individual is a potential lifesaver. Together, we move one step closer to a safer community where no life is lost due to lack of timely intervention

Seeing educators actively learn and engage in life-saving skills is truly inspiring.

🚑 *Empowering Those Who Protect Us* 🚦

It was a truly fulfilling experience to conduct a Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) training session for the dedicated officers of Kharghar Traffic Police Station. 

Our traffic police personnel are often the first responders at road traffic accidents and medical emergencies. Equipping them with *life-saving skills like CPR* can make a critical difference in those golden minutes before advanced medical care arrives.

During the session, we focused on:
✔️ Recognizing cardiac arrest early
✔️ Performing high-quality CPR
✔️ Understanding the importance of timely intervention
✔️ Hands-on practice to build confidence

This initiative was carried out along with our team from the *PICU, MGM Medical College, Kamothe* whose support and expertise made this session impactful and engaging.

The enthusiasm, participation, and commitment shown by the officers were truly commendable 👏

This initiative reinforces an important message — saving lives is a shared responsibility, and empowering community responders is a key step toward a safer society.
